note: Found by the nightly fuzz run on 2026-10-17. Chromium 0.064, copper 1.65 and arsenic 0.029 mg/L give a Hazard Index of 4.55 exactly, a tie at one decimal. Python's sum(), which from 3.12 compensates a sum of floats, came to 4.55 and printed '4.5'; the browser, adding the quotients one at a time, came to 4.550000000000001 and printed '4.6', as Python 3.10 and 3.11 did. Python was put right: every built-in sum() of floats that gwt-core.js mirrors now goes through utils.sum_in_order, which adds one value at a time as the browser does.
first_divergence: Non-carcinogenic Hazard Index 4.6 is at or above 1 (dominated by arsenic); chronic ingestion poses a potential health concern.
